title: Redwood / Securipharma - Security & Privacy Review
summary: Security review focused on data handling and privacy for PHI workflows. Discussed SOC 2 / ISO posture, SSO/RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data residency, and explicit confirmation that Redwood does not train models on customer data. Next steps: share SOC2/ISO report, privacy docs, sample audit logs, and schedule a technical follow-up to run a small PoC with isolated Dedicated environment.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood CSM), Mike (Securipharma CTO), Sara (Securipharma Security Lead), Jordan (Product), Anita (Compliance)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Mike: Mike here.
[00:14] Sara: Sara here.
[00:16] Jordan: Jordan, yep.
[00:18] Anita: Anita on compliance.
[00:20] Alex: Great. So today we wanted to run through Redwood's security posture and specifically how we handle data and privacy for PHI workflows, and answer anything about logs, encryption, and that "no training" guarantee. Priya will run through the technical bits.
[00:35] Priya: Thanks Alex. I'll start with a high-level overview of deployment modes - hosted, dedicated, and private VPC/on-prem - and then go into encryption and auditability.
[00:45] Priya: For customers with PHI you commonly look at Dedicated or Private options, that gives you network isolation and the ability to integrate with your KMS and key rotation policies.
[00:58] Sara: When you say integrate with our KMS, do you support bringing our keys - like AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault?
[01:06] Priya: Yes, we support BYOK patterns and integration with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP KMS. There's a tenant-level envelope encryption; Redwood stores encrypted model artifacts and we keep data at rest encrypted with customer-managed keys if you're on Private or Dedicated with KMS enabled. For hosted we offer a managed KMS option, and we can discuss contract terms for customer-managed keys.
[01:34] Mike: Is the key ever in Redwood's clear? How do you handle key access for ops and support?
[01:40] Priya: Keys are never stored unencrypted. For customer-managed keys we only see ciphertext. Access by ops is controlled via RBAC and audit logs; support access can be gated via Just-in-Time or approved breakglass processes - we can show our runbook.
[01:55] Anita: Can you provide details of your SOC 2 controls around key management and support access?
[02:02] Alex: We'll attach the SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO summary after the call. That doc covers control policies, access reviews, and support escalation.
[02:12] Sara: Great. On retention - our legal team requires that prompts and model responses containing PHI must not be retained beyond X days and in some cases never stored. How does Redwood handle prompt/content retention?
[02:25] Priya: By default, hosted API has configurable retention; for Dedicated and Private you get tenant-controlled retention and option for no retention (ephemeral only). We have a parameter at ingestion time to opt out of storage for model telemetry and prompts. For Hosted we've got configurable retention windows and you can request rolling deletion.
[02:44] Jordan: Is there any case where data is used to train models - like for improving models or fine-tuning? We need an explicit legal guarantee we won't train on our data.
[02:54] Alex: Short answer: Redwood does not use customer data to train our model weights. We provide a contractual no-training-on-customer-data clause. For Hosted, telemetry for service health may be collected but it's scrubbed and not used to update model parameters; for any use cases where data is fed into training pipelines, that requires explicit customer opt-in and separate agreement.
[03:16] Mike: Is that captured in the DPA?
[03:19] Alex: Yes - we'll include the DPA and the specific language about no-training.
[03:23] Sara: On PII and PHI detection, do you offer built-in redaction or classification?
[03:29] Priya: We have optional pre-processing hooks - you can run a redaction step in your environment before sending to Redwood, or use our built-in PII filters for hosted calls. For sensitive workflows we recommend client-side redaction (in your VPC) before transit.
[03:43] Anita: About transit: is TLS 1.2/1.3 enforced? Any mutual TLS support for Dedicated?
[03:49] Priya: Yes, TLS 1.2+ is enforced. For Dedicated and Private we support mTLS and private endpoints inside VPC peering or PrivateLink equivalents.
[04:01] Sara: Audit logs - we need immutable logs that show request id, user id, redwood-node, timestamp, and any admin actions. Can you export logs to our SIEM?
[04:12] Priya: We can stream audit logs to customer-owned S3/GCS/Azure blob or to SIEM via syslog/forwarder. Logs include request metadata, model used, response latency, who initiated it, and admin events. For Hosted we keep a managed retention window configurable per account; for Dedicated/Private you control retention and where logs are shipped.
[04:33] Jordan: Is the content of the prompts included in audit logs by default?
[04:37] Priya: By default no - prompt content can be included if you enable full payload logging. For PHI we recommend leaving content out of logs and logging only hashes or metadata to satisfy audit trails without storing sensitive content.
[04:51] Mike: Encryption at rest - can you confirm AES-256 and that hardware HSM is available for key storage?
[04:58] Priya: AES-256 at rest. HSM-backed KMS support is available for Private and some Dedicated deployments; for hosted we have managed KMS but we can discuss HSM-backed options under enterprise contract.
[05:11] Sara: For compliance, do you allow customer-side encryption where we encrypt payloads before sending and Redwood processes ciphertext? That would limit visibility but break model usefulness.
[05:21] Priya: You could do envelope encryption for metadata and select fields. End-to-end encryption of full payloads would prevent model from seeing content, so not viable if you need generation. We can support hybrid approaches where PII fields are tokenized client-side and replaced with placeholders before sending, preserving utility while protecting PHI.
[05:41] Mike: We have to confirm data residency - some EU patients' data must stay in EU. Do you have regional control?
[05:48] Alex: Yes, regional deployments are supported. For Dedicated/Private we can ensure data, logs, and keys live in a specific region and in customer VPC.
[05:57] Anita: How about data deletion guarantees - e.g., after we request deletion, is there a verifiable wipe across backups and caches?
[06:05] Priya: We have documented deletion flows. For ephemeral KV caches used during inference we scrub after session termination; for stored artifacts we perform logical deletion plus background compaction. For backups there is a retention policy and we can provide attestation and deletion timelines in the contract - we will include the technical deletion playbook.
[06:26] Sara: You mentioned KV cache - is that ever written to disk unencrypted?
[06:30] Priya: Cache shards are encrypted at rest and subject to the same KMS policies. For extra assurance we can pin KV to memory-only processes in Private deployments.
[06:41] Jordan: About SSO and RBAC - we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. Can you integrate with our IdP and map groups to roles?
[06:50] Alex: Yes, SAML and OIDC supported, SCIM for provisioning and group sync. RBAC is role-based with least-privilege roles; we support custom roles for admin, billing, developer, and read-only auditor roles.
[07:04] Sara: Are audit logs of admin actions immutable? Do you support tamper-evident storage?
[07:11] Priya: Logs are write-once in our managed stores and we can support archiving to customer-owned immutable buckets with object lock for tamper evidence.
[07:21] Mike: For technical deep dive - latency and model variants - we'll schedule a separate session. But one last question: if we do a PoC in Dedicated, can we limit access to a few IPs and have VPN to our data center?
[07:34] Priya: Yes, Dedicated supports IP allowlists, VPC peering, and private endpoints - we can set up VPN or Transit Gateway. We'll include connection playbook in the follow-up.

[07:45] Alex: Thanks everyone. Quick recap and next steps: we'll send SOC 2, ISO summary, DPA wording about no-training, and Priya will share architecture and sample logs. We'll aim to kick off PoC week of 2026-07-20.
[07:59] Anita: Thanks, that works.
[08:01] Mike: Appreciate it.
[08:03] Alex: End meeting.
notes: Customer highly focused on PHI handling and contractual no-training language
Priya emphasized Dedicated/Private for strong isolation
Alex to provide SOC2/ISO + DPA + legal wording for no-training
